response.sql: WITH diffs AS (SELECT event_status, amount - spent AS diff FROM budget WHERE amount - spent IS NOT NULL), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(diff) AS base FROM diffs) SELECT d.event_status AS status, AVG(d.diff) AS avg_diff, AVG(d.diff) - b.base AS diff_from_baseline FROM diffs d CROSS JOIN baseline b GROUP BY d.event_status, b.base HAVING b.base IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: Rows with a NULL event_status form their own group in the output, since the request does not say to exclude them.
The baseline is the average of (amount - spent) over all budget rows where that difference is non-NULL, with each row weighted equally. The per-status averages use the same filter.
If the baseline is NULL, no rows are returned. This happens only when no row has a non-NULL difference, and the HAVING clause enforces it.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude rows whose event_status is NULL from the per-status output, while still computing the baseline over all non-NULL differences.
alternatives.sql: WITH diffs AS (SELECT event_status, amount - spent AS diff FROM budget WHERE amount - spent IS NOT NULL), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(diff) AS base FROM diffs) SELECT d.event_status AS status, AVG(d.diff) AS avg_diff, AVG(d.diff) - b.base AS diff_from_baseline FROM diffs d CROSS JOIN baseline b WHERE d.event_status IS NOT NULL GROUP BY d.event_status, b.base HAVING b.base IS NOT NULL;
